keyChanges.title: ~100 Cybercabs staged at Dallas hub — still zero in paid public service
keyChanges.description: A Dallas-area robotaxi lot was photographed on the evening of Aug 23 with a large cluster of gold Cybercabs. TeslaNewswire and Basenor put the count at almost 100, roughly double the ~40 units Basenor says were reported at the same DFW hub in mid-June. The site matches Tesla's Irving, Texas robotaxi hub (documented in May city filings as a 24-acre DFW depot sized for up to 212 AVs). That is staging inventory, not a Cybercab city launch. Dallas/Houston Model Y unsupervised robotaxi has been live since April; none of these Cybercabs are in paid public service. A separate Aug 23 public-road clip still shows a no-steering-wheel, no-pedals Cybercab with a safety monitor in the passenger seat. Tesla's Sept 3 Austin date remains an invite-only launch EVENT — Teslarati and TeslaNorth both treat paid Cybercab rides that day as unconfirmed.

positive_signals: Photo/video from a Dallas Cybercab parking lot on Aug 23, amplified by TeslaNewswire as 'almost 100' units
Basenor reports the DFW hub count roughly doubled from ~40 in mid-June toward a depot designed for up to 212 AVs
Production-spec no-steering-wheel / no-pedals Cybercabs continue public-road validation ahead of the Sept 3 Austin event
negative_signals: Zero Cybercabs remain in paid public service; ~100 parked units are inventory, not a robotaxi print
'Almost 100' is a spotter/aggregator estimate, not a Tesla-confirmed count — Teslarati and TeslaNorth have not independently verified it
No-pedals road tests still require a human safety monitor in the passenger seat
Dallas already has Model Y unsupervised robotaxi; Cybercabs sitting at the hub have not replaced or expanded that paid fleet
Latest verified VIN floor is still ~2,172 (Aug 10) — most built Cybercabs are not in commercial use
Tesla is holding back Model Y robotaxi additions while waiting on Cybercab, so paid fleet growth is paused against a vehicle that is still not in service
Sept 3 is an influencer/invite event; paid Cybercab app availability that day is unconfirmed

keyChanges.title: Musk hypes WSJ praise of Supervised v14; 2026.26.6.2 still ships with no FSD merge
keyChanges.description: On Aug 22, Elon Musk amplified a Wall Street Journal review in which critic Dan Neil called Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) “amazing” and said he was “bewitched” after about two hours in a Model Y. TeslaNorth and Basenor both treated the write-up as a mainstream-press win, and TeslaNorth explicitly tied the drive to the current consumer stack: Hardware 4 on FSD (Supervised) v14.3.7 and Hardware 3 on v14.1 Lite via the unified 2026.21.6 package. That is not a software advance. The same day Tesla began rolling 2026.26.6.2, a Summer Update bug-fix build whose NotATeslaApp release notes still contain no FSD version and no v15 (or even v14) merge. TeslaFi-based fleet mix on NotATeslaApp shows the non-FSD 2026.26 branch already at ~45.7% of the tracked fleet versus ~29.4% on 2026.21; 2026.21.6 itself is ~27.8% of the fleet and remains the latest North America FSD drop. Consumer cars are still on supervised v14. Robotaxi-only v15, the ~40% track figure from IR, HW3’s Lite ceiling, and the lack of an official HW3 retrofit are all unchanged. A two-hour sample-of-one review does not move the ship date.

positive_signals: WSJ automotive critic Dan Neil described FSD (Supervised) as “amazing” and said it earned his confidence mile by mile after a ~2-hour Model Y drive, including rush-hour interstate lane centering and following distance.
Elon Musk amplified the review on X on Aug 22: “Try Tesla self-driving. Feels like magic.”
TeslaNorth confirms the current wide consumer rollout is still a unified 2026.21.6 package bringing v14.3.7 to HW4 and v14.1 Lite to HW3.
negative_signals: Neil himself framed the piece as a sample of one with limited evidence; this is a journalist impression of existing Supervised v14, not a new OTA or v15 consumer release.
Consumer FSD remains Supervised v14.3.7 (HW4) and v14.1 Lite (HW3). v15 is still not on customer-owned vehicles.
2026.26.6.2 (released Aug 22; TeslaFi ~0.8–1% of fleet) is another Summer Update point release with only bug/security fixes — NotATeslaApp lists no FSD version on this build.

The non-FSD 2026.26 branch is now the plurality of the TeslaFi fleet (~45.7%) while the FSD-carrying 2026.21 branch is ~29.4%, so a growing share of cars is on firmware that never received the latest FSD merge.
NotATeslaApp’s FSD index still shows 2026.21.6 (Aug 9) as the latest North America FSD drop; no v14.x or v15 consumer build landed on Aug 22–23.
IR’s v15 “step-change” claim and ~40% of robotaxi tracks, plus no official HW3 retrofit, were restated earlier this week and were not improved by this review or this OTA.

keyChanges.title: Aug 22–23 Tesla AI/FSD/Optimus hiring is empty of core engineering
keyChanges.description: Over 2026-08-22 to 2026-08-23, LinkedIn showed no new Tesla Autopilot, Tesla AI, or Optimus engineering requisitions. A past-24-hour Tesla (f_C=15564) search returned a single posting: Production Associate, Model Y, Body in Austin (posted ~4 hours ago). The only in-window FSD/AI-adjacent reqs are ops/program-management, not model work: an AI Safety Operator in Jacksonville, FL (posted ~2 days ago) whose JD is driving an engineering vehicle 6–8 hours a day for supervised-FSD camera/audio collection, plus a Technical Program Manager, Sensing Products in Palo Alto (posted ~2 days ago) owning vehicle-sensing hardware/software schedule, not Autopilot software. This continues last week's data-ops pulse (supervisors, mocap, simulation QA) rather than a core AI hiring surge. Tesla careers remains Akamai-blocked, so there is no official Optimus/FSD recount.

positive_signals: AI Safety Operator req is live in Jacksonville, extending FSD data-collection geography
Technical Program Manager, Sensing Products (Palo Alto) is a mid-senior hardware/software delivery role for vehicle sensing, not retail/service hiring
negative_signals: LinkedIn past-24-hour Tesla search: 1 job, and it is Model Y body production — not AI/robotics/FSD/Optimus
AI Safety Operator is entry-level data collection (valid license, 6–8 hours driving, start/stop recorders) — not Autopilot/Tesla AI engineering
No new Functional Safety, Autopilot software, Optimus AI, Dojo, or AI5 reqs identified in the Aug 22–23 window
Tesla.com/careers search and APIs return Akamai 403, so official AI-org headcount cannot be independently recounted
This is a continuation of last week's data-ops-not-engineering pattern, not a new scaling signal

keyChanges.title: Optimus manufacturing-adjacent reqs are live — still not a production-line ramp
keyChanges.description: Contrary to last week's 'no production-line Optimus pulse' read, LinkedIn now shows a thin cluster of Optimus manufacturing-adjacent roles that were still open on Aug 22–23 (LinkedIn stamps ~3 days ago): Robotics Manufacturing Engineer, Battery Manufacturing, Optimus (Austin) to take Optimus battery equipment from concept through launch — the JD itself says the architecture is in 'early development stages'; Process Technician, Optimus (Fremont) at $28.75–$37.41/hr covering production-line process, rework, and subsystem repair; Automated Systems Technician, Precision Machining, Optimus (Lathrop) for factory-automation install/repair; and Manufacturing Engineer, Battery Interconnects, Optimus (Palo Alto) whose body copy is generic EV battery interconnect (laser welding) and barely mentions the robot. These are individual engineer/technician reqs, not a wave of production associates. No weekend (past-24-hour) Optimus manufacturing adds. This is process-development and line-support hiring, not evidence Tesla is staffing a high-volume Optimus line.

positive_signals: Austin Robotics Manufacturing Engineer JD explicitly targets Optimus battery manufacturing equipment and high-volume automated lines
Fremont Process Technician, Optimus JD covers production-line process, yield/Cpk, and Optimus subsystem repair — a factory-floor role, not mocap/simulation
Lathrop Automated Systems Technician, Precision Machining, Optimus is factory-automation / machining support for the Optimus program
negative_signals: Austin JD still describes Optimus product architecture as in 'early development stages' — equipment concept-to-launch, not a staffed mass-production line
Four individual engineer/technician reqs is not a production-associate or shift-staffing wave
Palo Alto 'Battery Interconnects, Optimus' posting is largely a reused EV battery interconnect JD (laser welding, EV cost/performance) with Optimus only in the title
Zero new Optimus manufacturing roles in LinkedIn's past-24-hour Tesla filter (Aug 23)
No corroborating Teslarati, TeslaNorth, Tesla Oracle, or Optimusk.blog hiring articles in the Aug 22–23 window

keyChanges.title: Semi EOL cluster at Nevada factory — still no official volume 4 months after 'high-volume' start
keyChanges.description: Basenor, citing Sawyer Merritt (Aug 22) and TeslaNewswire video (Aug 23), reports multiple Tesla Semis clustered at the Sparks/Nevada Semi factory end-of-line staging area — the first visual hint of a modest output uptick since the dedicated high-volume line started April 29, 2026. Merritt’s own language is cautious (“at least a little bit”); Tesla still has not disclosed Semi production or delivery counts. The cluster is also the obvious staging pattern for Einride’s already-announced first trucks in September (500 units over 24 months), not proof of a 50,000-unit/year run-rate. Tesla has said the plant targets 50,000 annual capacity with “many thousands” by end of 2026 — even the high end of that would be a rounding error versus ~461.5k Q3 Street auto deliveries and Q2’s 480k print. Separately, Tesla Charging opened a 6-stall public Megacharger in Vernon, CA (industrial LA corridor), extending a still-thin Southern California Semi charging footprint beyond the earlier Ontario pad. No official Q3 2026 production/delivery print this window; Model Y L US deliveries remain October, so the 3-row adds no Q3 US volume.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Headlines read as a Semi production ramp. Reality is unquantified watcher video plus a 6-stall charger, 4 months after 'high-volume' start, with no official Semi units disclosed and first Einride deliveries already scheduled for September.

positive_signals: TeslaNewswire video shows multiple Semis queued at Nevada factory end-of-line (Aug 23), consistent with completed units awaiting delivery
Sawyer Merritt flagged at least a modest increase in Semi units coming off the line (Aug 22)
Tesla Charging officially posted a new 6-stall public Megacharger in Vernon, CA (Aug 21/22), adding LA-area Semi corridor charging
High-volume Semi line has been running since April 29, 2026; Einride 500-unit order still points to September first deliveries
negative_signals: Tesla has published no Semi production or delivery count; watcher language is explicitly 'at least a little bit,' not a confirmed inflection
EOL clustering is the expected staging pattern for Einride's already-announced September first trucks, not independent evidence of a 50k/year ramp
Four months after the 'high-volume' line started, output is still described as sluggish relative to the 50,000-unit annual capacity target
'Many thousands' of Semis by end of 2026 remains a rounding error vs Q3 Street ~461.5k auto deliveries and Q2's 480k
No official Q3 2026 vehicle production/delivery print; Model Y L US deliveries still October, so no Q3 US 3-row volume
China July retail already printed at 27,249 (exports masking weak domestic); August China retail not yet out

key_metrics.actual: Unquantified Semi EOL cluster; no official Semi unit count. Q3 Street still ~461.5k auto deliveries.
key_metrics.target: Semi factory 50,000/year capacity; 'many thousands' of Semis by end of 2026; Q3 auto likely down vs Q2 480k
key_metrics.trajectory: Visual Semi staging ahead of September Einride first deliveries; auto volume still the P&L, with no new Q3 print this window
